inputs.original_text: This is a crisis driven by decisions made by powerful governments, while ordinary people—especially those with the fewest resources to escape danger or rebuild—are left to absorb the consequences. When civilian areas and essential infrastructure are threatened, the damage reaches far beyond the battlefield, undermining the services people rely on. Talk of “just war” is hollow without accountability and real protection for civilians. The priority must be to stop the escalation and protect people, not make a wider regional war seem inevitable.
inputs.modified_text: Powerful governments are driving this crisis, while civilians with the least ability to flee or recover are made to bear the cost. Threats to civilian areas and essential infrastructure put people’s access to vital services at risk; that is not an acceptable side effect of political decisions. Claims of a “just war” mean little without accountability and meaningful protection for civilians. We should reject the idea that wider regional war is inevitable and demand de-escalation and protection for those most at risk.
